direction-type.words: Verse3: As I cam' in be Netherdale, at Turra merkat for tae fee,
I fell in wi' a fairmer chiel, fae the barnyards o' Delgaty.
Verse4: He promised me the twa best horses, ye ever set yer een upon;
Fin I gaed hame there tae the barnyards, there was now't but skin and bone.
Verse5: The auld black horse sat on his hunkers, the auld white meer lay on her wime.
For a' that I could up and cry, they widnae rise at yokin time.
Verse6: Meg MacPherson maks ma brose, an' her an me cannae agree.
First a mote and syne a knot, and aye the ither jilp o bree.
Verse7: Fin I ging tae the kirk on Sundays, monys the bonnie lass I see.
Sittin' by her faither's side, an winkin' ower the pews at me.
Verse8: Some can drink and nae be drunk, an' some can fecht and nae be slain.
But I can coort anither man's lass, and aye be welcom tae my ain.
Verse9: Ma cannie noo it is brunt oot, the snotters fairly on the wane.
Sae fare ye weel ye barnyards, ye'll ne'er catch me here again.
